fix(ui): remove fabricated latency/benchmark metrics

Nothing in Beni measures validator latency, and the contract uses a list
check, not a bloom filter. These were invented numbers presented as fact:

- Dashboard KPI 'Validator latency 28ms / p95 41ms' -> real 'Per-tx cap'
  pulled from the on-chain rules (or '·' when no contract is deployed)
- Security page 'What happens in 28ms' -> 'Every spend, checked four ways'
- Pipeline: dropped the fake per-step millisecond column and the
  '12 addresses · bloom filter' line; descriptions now match the validator
- SecurityStats '28ms median validator latency' -> '1 block to freeze a
  rogue agent' (a real property of the freeze path)

feat(core+cli+mcp): S+7 — flyway_discover completes the 9-tool surface

Discovery is the one pre-trust tool: it helps a Source find potential
peers before proposing recognition. Nothing it returns is trusted —
directory entries are informational pointers, not attestations. A
directory that lies can only waste your time, never forge an identity:
you still verify at recognition. So entries are unsigned and discover
performs no signature checks. This is the last stubbed tool — 9 of 9 now
wired.

Core (discover.ts)
- FlywayDirectory / FlywayDirectoryEntry types + FLYWAY_DIRECTORY_SCHEMA
  (JSON Schema). An entry needs only did + sourceName; mode, capabilities,
  repoUrl, description are optional hints.
- flywayDiscover({ directory, query? }): pure query. No query → all
  entries; query starting `did:` → exact DID match; otherwise
  case-insensitive substring over did / sourceName / capabilities /
  description, in directory order.
- parseFlywayDirectory(raw): validates shape (schemaVersion, entries,
  per-entry did/sourceName/mode/capabilities), rejects duplicate DIDs,
  returns a defensively-copied typed document.

Transport: v0.1 reads a LOCAL directory file. Fetching a directory over
http(s) — the first genuinely non-local-fs operation — is a reserved
seam: the directory shape is defined now so a remote fetcher drops in
later without changing the query logic (parallels ADR-0008 reserving
remote signal transports). A URL source is refused with a clear message,
never silently treated as a path.

CLI
- `flyway discover --directory <path> [query] [--json]`. Read-only,
  needs no identity. Loads a YAML/JSON directory file, parses, filters,
  prints (human or --json).

MCP
- handleDiscover replaces the last not-implemented stub; stateless (the
  caller supplies the directory document; the server does no fs/network
  I/O), parses + filters + returns matches. Refreshed the handlers test
  that asserted discover was unimplemented; added unknown-tool coverage.

Tests: core +16, cli +7, mcp +3. 355 passed workspace-wide (233 core /
90 cli / 23 mcp / 9 agent).

Smoke: list-all, free-text filter, exact-DID lookup, and http-URL refusal
all behave. The protocol surface is complete.

build: migrate pnpm settings to pnpm-workspace.yaml (pnpm 10+/11 compat)

pnpm 11 no longer reads the "pnpm" field from package.json, so the
peerDependencyRules that suppressed resolution of the harness package's
private, unpublished optional peer (@murmurations-ai/murmurations-harness)
were being ignored — `pnpm install` then 404'd on that dep and left
node_modules unpopulated, breaking every build/test until a manual
workaround.

Moves the settings to their new home in pnpm-workspace.yaml:
- peerDependencyRules.ignoreMissing — keeps install from resolving the
  unpublished harness peer (harness is excluded from builds/tests anyway).
- autoInstallPeers: false — matches the lockfile (avoids a frozen-install
  config-mismatch error after the pnpm upgrade).
- allowBuilds: { esbuild: true } — approves esbuild's install script
  (pulled in by vitest), clearing ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS.

Removes the now-dead "pnpm" field from package.json.

Verified: a clean `pnpm install` then `pnpm -r --filter
'!@murmurations-ai/flyway-harness' build && … test` runs green (329
tests) with no CI=true or --config workarounds. Lockfile unchanged.
